title: Banner Band dates, Black Eagle band and substitutes
summary: Duhé was with the band until the 1927 flood, brought in Bunk and New Orleans substitutes, and also ran the Black Eagle band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And when was that Banner Band about? When were you with it and when was Bunk with it?
Well, I was, I was there until the 27th. I don't know how that's done when the flood, the flood ran us up in Texas. And the flood took water. I stayed there about eight years, I can remember.
When do you think, how long you started there in 1921 or so maybe then? I guess so around the 20s, yeah. When was Bunk in it then, when you joined?

Not when I first joined, but after I was in there, well, I got him. You don't know just 20 joined then? No, I don't know when. I used to go to New Orleans and get substitutes, you know, with plays, just like I did in the Black Eagle. Black Eagle, I went and got Earl Humphrey and John Joseph, Irvin Joseph on drum. Irvin, that's my cousin. Yeah, Tom Benton.
Oh, he had banjo or guitarist. Yeah, well, I got reinforced those country bands. I was bunking the Black Eagle band too for a while. Yeah, uh-huh. With you, same time as you? No, not same time.
Later, I guess. Mox was in the same time. Mox, another homeboy. Yeah. Yeah, sack of mute.
T-Boy was playing with that band once too. Where's T-Boy? T-Boy Rene? You know, you remember Johnny French, bro?

Oh, yeah, you know Johnny French. You remember Johnny French and Marshall, one where his trumpet plays? Oh, yes, yes, I do. Johnny French appreciates banjo, he's got a big choice. That's a good rap. Oh, well.
